items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: When Leonard Feather moved out there, I think he got a job with the L.A. Times, presumably to write a lot about jazz.

ctx.x: Well I guess there’s not nearly as many places for the young musicians just out of school to go and really hone their craft.

Well unless they’re in New York City, I mean there’s just so much music in New York, and the other places it’s just dried up, although I’m told that there’s certain pockets around the country. Certainly not Los Angeles. There’s very little out there. When Leonard Feather moved out there, I think he got a job with the L.A. Times, presumably to write a lot about jazz. There wasn’t a heck of a lot. I mean one person had opened and then that would be a big event. Well the distances are great. But what’s terrible here…
Did you make the scene at 52nd Street?
